parameters.query:
-- The polling marker and the allowlist in one round trip, so the rest of the
-- workflow never has to go back to the database for a single message.
SELECT
  -- After a week with no messages Telegram starts numbering them again from a
  -- random point, which can be lower than the marker we kept. Asking from the
  -- old marker would then never return anything. Nothing handled for 6 days
  -- means we ask from the start of whatever is waiting instead.
  coalesce((SELECT CASE WHEN updated_at < now() - interval '6 days' THEN 0
                        ELSE value::bigint END
              FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'telegram_offset'), 0)
    AS next_offset,
  coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
              'telegram_user_id', u.telegram_user_id,
              'user_id',          u.id,
              'name',             coalesce(u.display_name, u.email),
              'role',             u.role))
              FROM users u
             WHERE u.telegram_user_id IS NOT NULL
               AND u.removed_at IS NULL), '[]'::jsonb)
    AS allowlist;

-- Nothing is stored unless the sender is on the allowlist and we have both a
-- link and a title, so a stray message cannot put an item in the newsletter.
WITH me AS (
    SELECT $1::text        AS tg_id,
           nullif($2, '')  AS url,
           nullif($3, '')  AS title,
           nullif($4, '')  AS publisher,
           $5::timestamptz AS published_at,
           nullif($6, '')  AS note,
           nullif($7, '')  AS body
),
person AS (
    SELECT u.id FROM users u JOIN me ON u.telegram_user_id = me.tg_id
     WHERE u.removed_at IS NULL
),
-- read before the insert below, so we can tell "saved" from "already had it"
seen AS (
    SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM items i JOIN me ON i.canonical_url = canonicalise_url(me.url)) AS already
),
stored AS (
    INSERT INTO items (source_id, source_url, canonical_url, title, publisher,
                       published_at, excerpt, raw_text, status, captured_by, fetched_at)
    SELECT (SELECT id FROM sources WHERE type = 'manual' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),
           me.url, me.url, me.title, me.publisher, me.published_at, me.note,
           me.body, 'new', (SELECT id FROM person), now()
      FROM me
     WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM person)
       AND me.url IS NOT NULL
       AND me.title IS NOT NULL
    ON CONFLICT (canonical_url) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id, duplicate_of
)
SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM person) AS allowed,
       (SELECT id FROM stored)       AS item_id,
       (SELECT duplicate_of FROM stored) AS duplicate_of,
       (SELECT already FROM seen)    AS already_known;

-- One statement, so an item is never marked summarised without a summary.
-- When the AI did not answer there is nothing to save, and the item stays new
-- for the scheduled summarisation to pick up.
WITH s AS (
    INSERT INTO summaries (item_id, language, text, provider, model)
    SELECT $1::bigint, 'fi', btrim($2), $3, $4
     WHERE nullif(btrim($2), '') IS NOT NULL
    ON CONFLICT (item_id, language) DO UPDATE
       SET text = EXCLUDED.text, generated_at = now()
    RETURNING item_id
)
UPDATE items SET status = 'summarised' WHERE id = (SELECT item_id FROM s);

-- /schedule on its own shows the times. With times it replaces them, and off
-- stops automatic checking. /reschedule does the same, for changing the times. Anything else is answered, not saved, so a typo
-- cannot switch the checking off by accident.
WITH arg AS (
    SELECT lower(btrim(coalesce($1, ''))) AS a
),
wanted AS (
    SELECT CASE
             WHEN a = '' THEN NULL
             WHEN a IN ('off', 'pois') THEN 'off'
             WHEN a ~ '^([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3])[:.][0-5][0-9]([ ,]+([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3])[:.][0-5][0-9])*$' THEN
               (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT to_char(replace(t, '.', ':')::time, 'HH24:MI'), ' '
                                  ORDER BY to_char(replace(t, '.', ':')::time, 'HH24:MI'))
                  FROM regexp_split_to_table(a, '[ ,]+') AS t)
             ELSE 'invalid'
           END AS v
      FROM arg
),
saved AS (
    UPDATE app_settings s
       SET value = w.v, updated_at = now()
      FROM wanted w
     WHERE s.key = 'collection_times'
       AND w.v IS NOT NULL AND w.v <> 'invalid'
    RETURNING s.value
)
SELECT coalesce((SELECT value FROM saved),
                (SELECT value FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'collection_times')) AS times,
       coalesce((SELECT v = 'invalid' FROM wanted), false) AS invalid,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM saved) AS changed;
